You walk for what seems like years through the endless, glittering expanse. Eventually, you reach a house built out of the same vibrant colour as the rest of the landscape. This must be your destination. Inside, you find a small red-haired woman in a green dress. She offers you a seat and makes you tea. You ask about the portal and its peculiar destination, and she speaks of the realm's transportative powers. You plead with her to seal the portal, lest the Myriad Gentleman find it and seize this land for his own. The threat to her home rather sobers her, and she agrees to close the realm off for a time. She walks you to the portal. With her at your side, it takes but a few minutes.
In your Campaign Log, record that "you took tea with the ruler of a strange dimension." Complete Strange Portal. Each investigator at this location moves to Paris. Flip this card over and add it to the victory display.

You spend days entreating the being, to no avail. On the third night, though, you dream of crimson and white, and of an unknowable creature, unimaginably vast in dimensions you cannot comprehend, its gaze fixed on you. You awaken soaked in sweat, with a single word fixed in your head: "Go." You leave Sydney early the next day. It's not until you've reached dry land on the far side of the ocean that you begin to feel a strange influence tingling up your spine...
Move to Shanghai. Put the set-aside Wings of Damakairon asset into play under your control. For the remainder of this scenario, it does not take up a body slot. Complete Entreating the Gods. Remove this card from the game.

You find the cause of the Myriad's interest: the ruins of the Colosseum. Pushing past barriers and signs marked "DANGER", you find yourself standing in the arena's center, gazing on a split in the fabric of time. It's clear from the paraphernalia surrounding it that the Myriad have been trying to harness this breach—perhaps you can finish their work yourself.
Put the set-aside Forestall Fate asset into play under your control. For the remainder of this scenario, it does not take up an arcane slot. Complete Up To Something. Remove this card from the game.

You cut your way through the members of the expedition, each compelled to slice at you with whatever they have to hand—pocket knives, archaeological gear, shards of rock. You pant with the exertion, finding yourself momentarily clear, but still the strange aurora circles, poking and prodding at your mind. You must find a way to stop it.
You must decide (choose one): You retreat, while you still have that option. Each investigator at your location may move to a connecting location. Flip this card back over and restore it to 1 health. You find the expedition before too long. They've set up a dig site near the centre of the strange crater. You settle in to a good vantage point, hoping to spy what's going on. Before too long, there's a shout from the dig site. People—some of them, but not all, being versions of The Myriad Gentleman—start to gather around, a commotion builds, and then all go stock still. A strange colour, something you can only even call colour by analogy, drifts from the hole, flowing around the archaeological group. As one, they turn, and start moving towards you.
Put the set-aside Brainwashed Expedition enemy into play at Tunguska. Flip this card back over. For the remainder of the game, it cannot be flipped over again.

back.name: The Tunguska Event
back.text: No one really knows what happened at Tunguska. Well, perhaps not no one. The Myriad certainly seem to know something. At the end of the round, investigators at Tunguska spend 2 clues, as a group: Flip this card over and resolve its text. Task – Uncover the Myriad's plans for Tunguska.

front.text:
The Myriad has ties to the Bureau too, as it turns out. You find yourself playing cat and mouse for a while, digging up evidence of the Myriad's plans while avoiding their attempts to ensnare you in red tape. In the end, you receive a lukewarm missive stating that the FBI are looking into the matter, and that you should stay out of it. Disappointing. Still, you've made a few contacts, and should be able to call in a few favours when needed.
Add the set-aside Agency Strike Team event to your hand. For the remainder of this scenario, you are considered to own this card. Complete Higher Powers. Remove this card from the game.

front.text:
The job is simple enough: break into an eccentric millionaire's private collection, liberate a couple of pieces, drop them off at a local bakery. The package comes through two weeks later, a silver pendant and a message: "We will be there."
In your Campaign Log, record that "you have advanced the schemes of the Silver Twilight Lodge." Put the set-aside Ionian Pendant into play under your control. For the remainder of this scenario, it does not take up an accessory slot. Complete The Devil You Know. Remove this card from the game.

Communicating with the Order of the Silver Twilight is difficult, but not impossible. They offer you their aid, 
in exchange for a small favor.

front.text: High in the Himalayas, an order of monks resists the machinations of the Myriad. Perhaps if you visit them, they could provide some assistance. There's only one small problem... Spawn the set-aside Savage Yeti enemy at the Himalayas. Task – Deal with the Savage Yeti.

Aforgomon is not the only entity with interests in the timestream. An ancient spirit sits in opposition to it, and you've heard enough tales of fevered dreams from Sydney to have a good idea of where you might find it. Attach the set-aside Distant Entity asset to Sydney. Task – Make contact with a distant entity.

An organisation like the FBI is unlikely to believe stories of time travel, monsters and forgotten gods. The Myriad has its fingers in a lot of pies, though; if enough of these connections were shown to the Bureau, perhaps they could be convinced. Attach Exposition to San Francisco. Place 1 resource on each of Mexico City, Istanbul and Shanghai. Task – Expose the operations of the Myriad.

Rumors abound of an ancient arcane tome, recently acquired by the British Library. That kind of power could come in handy, but it will surely be closely guarded. Put the set-aside The British Library into play, revealed location side faceup. Task – Steal a tome from the British Library.

The Silver Twilight Lodge is something of a fixture in Arkham. Secretive, yes, and undoubtedly dangerous... But powerful. Power you can use, perhaps. Attach the set-aside Contacting the Lodge treachery to Arkham, Massachusetts. Task – Win the favor of the Silver Twilight Lodge.

The Myriad Gentleman, you have been reliably informed, has been spotted in Italy no fewer than half a dozen times. You don't doubt that he's in most places, if you look hard enough, but this seems an unusual amount of attention. Attach the set-aside Scheme of the Myriad to Rome. Search the encounter deck and discard pile for 2 copies of The Myriad Gentleman and spawn them in Rome. Task – Find whatever the Myriad is after in Rome.

You understand now. All the strange things that happened—the unexplained assistance you received—that was all you. This you, helping set things up for past you. ...You should probably get started on that. Task – Remove all resources from .

front.flavor_text: When you land, you have a brief moment to take in your surroundings, to learn what you can about this place, and each time you do you can hold on for a little longer. Perhaps, with enough focus, you can learn to navigate this place a little—enough to find a way out, at least.

back.name: A Path Appears
back.text:
Swimming through time and space, you've gotten something of a feel for navigating distant times. As you float along, you hold an image in your head—home, blessed home—and begin to craft a path.
Put the set-aside The Timestream and Arkham, Massachusetts (Present Day?) locations into play.

front.flavor_text: Time itself seems to be fighting you—forcing you from your intended path—but you struggle on. Arkham is within reach.

back.name: Home
back.text:
You land, splayed out in the streets of Easttown. The old, crooked buildings, the passers-by giving you suspicious looks—this is it. Arkham, Massachusetts, 1925.
R1.

front.flavor_text: Your flight is a little more controlled now. Tenuous, still, and chaotic, but you're gaining a loose understanding of this... place?

back.name: Time Turned Dark
back.text:
The air, such as it is, surrounding you shifts and turns. Fragments of the Myriad's ritual echo outward from their nexus, poisoning the well of time around you.
Discard each non-weakness treachery card in play. Each investigator at an Adrift location moves to a random other Adrift location. Shuffle the set-aside Paradox encounter set into the encounter deck, along with the encounter discard pile. Place 1 doom on agenda 3a as it is revealed.

front.flavor_text: The worlds around you are darker now, colder not in temperature but in the pressure they exert on your soul. The tampering of the Myriad can be felt throughout time and space.

back.name: Reality Changes
back.text:
Time sticks. For a moment—though what is a moment without time?—all is still, unnaturally so. Then, inevitably, you lurch out of reality and back into the maelstrom of intermingling times.
For each Adrift location occupied by an investigator, find the version of that location that was removed from the game and swap them (all tokens and cards at the former location are now considered to be at the new location). Do not place clues on the new locations as they are revealed. Discard each non-weakness treachery card in play. Each investigator at an Adrift location moves to a random other Adrift location. Place 1 doom on agenda 4a as it is revealed.

front.flavor_text: You fall through time, through existence, bouncing between bygone ages and far-flung futures. Your flight is barely controlled, try as you might to grasp on to passing days.

back.name: Falling Still

back.name: Glimpse of Things to Come
back.text:
Energy twists and roils through the auditorium, the unbound rifts expanding uncontrollably. Cultists scatter, abandoning their implements in a desperate attempt to preserve their own lives. You hold fast. You've witnessed your past self plunge headlong into the timestream, but you've learnt a lot since then. Enough to be able to navigate the flow of existence, and enough to know that Aforgomon won't rest now that the ritual has failed. This breach is the in-road it needs to unmake time itself. You step once more into the timestream, ready to do battle with a god.
(R1).

front.flavor_text: Your job is complicated by the fact that the school you broke into a year ago—well, today—is... gone. There's not even a space where it should be. Something here is very wrong.

back.name: A Riddle of Sorts
back.text:
The space around where the school should be iswrong. Space bends in an unnatural manner, your steps not bringing you to where they should. So, it should just be a matter of moving to where you cannot... And sure enough, after doing the impossible, Mount Hollyoke ripples into view, the strange dimension around it slipping away.
Put Front Gates, Sports Field, Children's Playground and Side Building into play. Move each investigator and enemy in play to Sports Field. Remove Featureless Streets from the game. If the investigators used the school's front door, put Rear Corridors into play. Otherwise, put Front Hallway into play.

front.flavor_text: A greenish, shimmering barrier surrounds the school, letting nothing through. You'll need to use a different entrance to your past self, and not disturb the barrier too much lest they—you—notice.

back.name: Breaking the Boundary
back.text:
Preparing the components you've gathered and uttering a familiar incantation, you step into the barrier, parting it wide enough to allow you passage.
If the Myriad recruited a cruel sorcerer, spawn the set-aside Estravius Malone at the revealed Interior location. If you advanced by entering the Front Hallway:
As you step through the school's front doors, you are stopped in your tracks by the sight of a colossal, slumbering beast blocking your path.
Put the set aside Cafeteria and Principal's Office locations into play. Spawn the set-aside Hound of Unmaking at the Front Hallway. Shuffle each set-aside copy of Stirring Titan into the encounter deck. Advance to Act 3a – Big and Ugly. If you advanced by entering the Rear Corridors:
You slip into the school through the back and spot a door at the end of the hall wrapped in purplish energy.
Put the set aside Classroom locations into play. Attach the set aside Unstable Warding story asset to Rear Corridors. If there is at least one token in the chaos bag, place 1 horror on Unstable Warding. Advance to Act 3a – Doorway to the Unknown.

front.flavor_text: Elsewhere on the grounds of this school, your past self is trying to break down the boundary too. They must not know you're here.

back.name: Predestined Progress
back.text:
The emerald barrier ripples as elsewhere, a neutralising ritual is performed. That should make things easier.
Check your Campaign Log. If the investigators used the school's front door, advance to Act 2c – Hellish Hound. Otherwise, advance to Act 2c – Warded Way.

back.name: A Familiar Chaos
back.text:
Time is running out, or running together, or simply falling apart. Nothing around you is stable. Ancient things become new and effect precedes cause. You grit your teeth and keep fighting, knowing you can't hold on much longer.

front.flavor_text: As the ritual reaches a crescendo, you feel the days of your life stacked up against one another. You can see your past of blissful innocence, every day spent fighting this terible cult, and through it all the gaze of Aforgomon's three eyes. You rail against it, fighting on even as time around you melts away.

back.name: All Times Are One
back.text:
You can't hold on any longer. You let go, as time falls apart.
Each remaining investigator is defeated.

back.text:

The ward is powerful, the energy crackling through it enough to power a small city. Nevertheless, you manage to disrupt its flow, grounding the magic and allowing you passage.

You step through the now unprotected doorway and find yourself face to face, once again, with the Myriad Gentleman. Wearing decadent ceremonial robes, he assumes a defensive stance, drawing sigils in the air before him.
Put each set-aside Ritual Circle location into play. Spawn the set aside The Myriad Gentleman (The High Priest) at the Ritual Circle (A Harnessed Future). Advance to Act 4a – Breaking the Circles.

front.flavor_text: You're back in Arkham, a year wiser and a year more worn down. You know how this goes—the ritual has begun, and you need to put a stop to it.

back.name: Breaking the Boundary
back.text:
Preparing the components you've gathered and uttering an incantation, you step into the barrier, parting it wide enough to allow you passage.
In your Campaign Log, record that the boundary is broken. Next to this, record the time. If you advanced by entering the Front Hallway:
As you step through the school's front doors, you are stopped in your tracks by the sight of a colossal, slumbering beast blocking your path.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators used the school's front door. Remove Rear Corridors from the game. Put the set-aside Cafeteria and Principal's Office locations into play. Spawn the set-aside Hound of Unmaking at the Front Hallway. Shuffle each set-aside copy of Stirring Titan into the encounter deck. Advance to Act 2a – Big and Ugly. If you advanced by entering the Rear Corridors:
You slip into the school through the back and spot a door at the end of the hall wrapped in purplish energy.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators snuck into the back of the school. Remove Front Hallway from the game. Put each of the set-aside Classroom locations into play. Attach the set-aside Unstable Warding story asset to Rear Corridors. Advance to Act 2a – Doorway to the Unknown.

front.flavor_text: The school hall has been transformed—three huge ritual circles cover most of the floor, crackling with energy. Flashes of other times assault your senses. You have to break this circle before it is too late.

back.name: Glimpse of Things to Come
back.text:
Fighting past the cultists guarding the circle, you seize a passing moment and use it to disrupt the flow of temporal energies. The backlash is immense—as the circle slowly shatters, fragments of history explode out at you. You weather the storm, turning towards the other two circles.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators broke the first circle. Next to this, record the time. (R3).

front.flavor_text: The Myriad are here in force. As the very fabric of your existence wears thin, the Gentleman and the creatures that serve him stand against you in ever greater numbers.

back.name: Chaos Temporalis
back.text:
Time is running out, or running together, or simply falling apart. Nothing around you is stable. Ancient things become new and effect precedes cause. How much longer do you have before you too succumb to time?
Each investigator reveals a random token from the chaos bag. Each investigator who reveals a symbol loses 1 action and gets +1 skill value during skill tests until the end of the round. Each other investigator gains 1 action and gets –1 skill value during skill tests until the end of the round.

front.flavor_text: As the ritual reaches a crescendo, you feel the days of your life stacked up against one another. You can see your past, even glimpses of days yet to come, and through all of them the terrible gaze of Aforgomon's three eyes. It seems to mock you as your minutes merge and twist together.

back.name: Time Shatters
back.text:
And just like that, time falls apart.
Each remaining investigator is defeated.

back.name: Time Breaking Slowly
back.text:
Time stretches out ever longer, then snaps together in unfamiliar configurations. The ritual progresses, and chronology is becoming unstuck...

Place this card next to the agenda deck as a reminder, then advance to agenda 2a.

back.name: Myriad Encounters
back.text:
If there are 4 resources on Unstable Warding:
The ward is powerful, the energy crackling through it enough to power a small city. Nevertheless, you manage to disrupt its flow, grounding the magic and allowing you passage.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators dispelled the ward. Next to this, record the time. Remove Unstable Warding from the game. If the investigators unleashed chaos:
The energy of the broken ward ripples out, disturbing and destabilising the Myriad's ritual.
Place 4 clues on Ritual Circle (A Harnessed Future) as it enters play. Then, remove 1 clues from Ritual Circle (A Harnessed Future) for each resource on Unstable Warding. However you advanced:
You step through the now unprotected doorway and find yourself face to face, once again, with the Myriad Gentleman. Wearing decadent ceremonial robes, he assumes a defensive stance, drawing sigils in the air before him.
Put the set aside Ritual Circle (A Harnessed Future) into play. Spawn the set aside The Myriad Gentleman (The High Priest) at the Ritual Circle. Advance to Act 3a – Breaking the Circle.

back.name: Physical Education
back.text:
If you spent clues to advance:
You augment the school bell with some of the ritual components you've gathered from around the school. It lets out a piercing screech, startling the Hound and sending it bounding away towards the back of the school.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators repelled the Hound of Unmaking. Next to this, record the time and the amount of damage on the Hound of Unmaking. Remove the Hound of Unmaking from the game. If you defeated the Hound of Unmaking:
The beast lets out a haunting wail, and the whole corridor shakes as its form collapses to the ground. You let out a breath you didn't realise you were holding, and get to work moving the immense body out of your way.
In your Campaign Log, record that the investigators put down the Hound of Unmaking. Next to this, record the time. However you advanced: Put the set aside Ritual Circle (Gateway to the Past) location into play. Advance to Act 3a – Breaking the Circle.

back.text:
If it is act 1:
A fine manor house towers over the estate. You spend some time seeking a way inside, though attempts at subtlety are rendered moot as the front door simply opens, and a man ambles out to meet you.
Each investigator loses each of their clues. Remember that "he is ready for you." Advance to act 1b. If it is act 2 or 3:

back.text:
As you explore the manor's garden, a tall man in a fine suit strolls out to meet you, seemingly unconcerned at you ransacking his property. "A shame," he sighs. "You just can't get the staff these days." You try to ask him why he'd plotted your demise, but he cuts you off. "No, no, no time for that. It's too close now, there's nothing for it. I'm going to have to finish you off myself." He draws a dagger and advances on you.

back.name: First Amongst Equals
back.text:
You've found all kinds of documents around this awful manor. References to a ritual, a unification, happening tonight. Mentions of this man, Joseph Baxter, the Myriad Gentleman, and a boon granted by a being known as Aforgomon. Finally, you find a heavy brass key in a hidden drawer. It opens the door to the manor's study with a low creak. Inside, you find the man, again, though this time he's prying an ornate sword off of the wall. "If you want something doing," he says, smiling slightly at his sort-of joke.
Reveal the Study. Spawn the set-aside The Myriad Gentleman (Master of the House) and 1 copies of The Myriad Gentleman (Thousandfold Man) at the Study.

# Ages Unwound

## Time Takes its Toll

*"I was well acquainted with Milwarp over a term of years.

But my recollection of the man is becoming strangely

blurred, like an image in a misted mirror. His dark,

half-alien personality, his preoccupation with the occult,

his immense knowledge of Eastern life and lore, are things

I remember with such effort and vagueness as attends the

recovery of a dream. Sometimes I almost doubt that he

ever existed. It is as if the man, and all that pertains to him,

were being erased from human record by some mysterious

acceleration of the common process of obliteration."

<right>--- Clark Ashton Smith, "The Chain of Aforgomon"*

<left>*Ages Unwound* is a fan-made campaign for Arkham Horror: The Card Game for 1–4 players.

## Additional Rules and Clarifications

### <black>Alert

Each time an investigator fails a skill test while attempting to evade

an enemy with the alert keyword, after applying all results for

that skill test, that enemy performs an attack against the evading

investigator. An enemy does not exhaust after performing an alert

attack. This attack occurs whether the enemy is engaged with the

evading investigator or not.

### <black>Story Cards

Story cards serve as an avenue for additional narrative and typically appear as the reverse side of another scenario card. When you are instructed to resolve a story card, simply read its story text and resolve its game text.

### <black>Swarming X

An enemy with the swarming X keyword is actually a pack of

enemies operating in unison. After you put an enemy with the

swarming X keyword into play, place the top X cards of your deck

facedown underneath the enemy as swarm cards, without looking

at them. The enemy they are underneath is called the “host enemy.”

Some scenario card effects may also instruct a player to add swarm

cards to an enemy. This is done using the same process.

<bullet><emsp> If it is ever unclear which investigator should add swarm cards,

<emsp> the lead investigator does so.

<bullet><emsp> Each swarm card underneath the host enemy acts as a separate

<emsp> instance of that enemy for most purposes. Each swarm card

<emsp> has the same values and text as its host card. (For example, if

<emsp> an investigator is engaged with a host enemy with 2 swarm

<emsp> cards underneath it, that investigator is engaged with 3 enemies

<emsp> in total.)

<bullet><emsp> Each swarm card attacks separately when enemies attack during

<emsp> the enemy phase. Once the host enemy and all of its swarm

<emsp> cards have attacked during this step, exhaust all of them.

<bullet><emsp> Each swarm card can be attacked or dealt damage separately,

<emsp> but the host enemy cannot be defeated while it still has swarm

<emsp> cards underneath it. When a swarm card is defeated, any excess

<emsp> damage may be dealt to another swarm card underneath the

<emsp> same host enemy or to the host enemy itself. *(For example,

<emsp> Tony Morgan uses a Chicago Typewriter to attack The Myriad

<emsp> Gentleman with 2 swarm cards. The attack deals 3 damage. The

<emsp> first 2 points of damage defeat 1 of the 2 swarm cards, so the

<emsp> excess point of damage may be dealt to another swarm card,

<emsp> damaging but not defeating it.)*

<bullet><emsp> Anytime a swarm card leaves play, place it on the bottom of its

<emsp> owner’s deck. If you are unsure of the owner of the swarm card,

<emsp> you may look at it to determine its owner.

<bullet><emsp> The host enemy and all of its swarm cards move, engage,

<emsp> and exhaust as a single entity. (For example, if a host enemy

<emsp> or any of its swarm cards are evaded, all of them exhaust and

<emsp> become disengaged.)

## Changes for Solo Play

A few effects in Ages Unwound will instruct you to interact with another investigator's deck. To simulate this in true solo play, construct a dummy deck out of the following cards:

<bullet><emsp>Guardian: .45 Automatic, Beat Cop, Emergency Aid, On the

Hunt, Vicious Blow

<bullet><emsp>Seeker: Hawk-Eye Folding Camera, Old Book of Lore,

Barricade, Connect the Dots, Deduction

<bullet><emsp>Rogue: Burglary, Lockpicks, Narrow Escape, Sneak

Attack, Quick Thinking

<bullet><emsp>Mystic: Rite of Seeking, Shrivelling, Dark Prophesy, Drawn to

the Flame, Fearless

<bullet><emsp>Survivor: Gravedigger's Shovel, Rabbit's Foot, Hiding

Spot, Scrounge for Supplies, Rise to the Occasion

Remove any cards of your class from this deck, as well as any cards you have at least one copy of in your deck. If you do not own any of the cards on this list, make appropriate replacements from your collection. *(Each class has 2 assets, 2 events and 1 skill, representing the core of that class. Avoid must-have or always-useful cards such as Lone Wolf.)*

Whenever you are instructed to interact with another investigator's deck, instead interact with the dummy deck. When a card from the dummy deck would leave play, instead shuffle it back into the dummy deck.

## Prologue

*The night's chill has reached your bones, soaking through your layers of warm clothing and settling on your soul. Your eyes, by now accustomed to the dim moonlight, spot no movement on the abandoned street. It's long past midnight. It must be past 1am by now.

The call had been rather questionable---a muffled, distorted voice, entreating you to meet it at midnight, that the fate of the world depended on it. Outlandish, yes, but the caller knew things, things that almost no-one knows about you. It wasn't quite blackmail, but rather a promise of trustworthiness. A promise that everything would be explained soon.

You feel a little foolish as you trudge home. Like some cruel trick has been played upon you. Probably you shouldn't have gone, but something made you want to believe the voice on the other end of the phone. Foolish.

Bright, flickering light almost blinds you. You blink rapidly, and as your eyes adjust the blinding hues resolve into an image of fire and fury. Your home is ablaze, an inferno so fierce and hot that it couldn't not be deliberate. Somebody trying to kill you? But why?

And if this is an attempt on your life, what does that make the peculiar call you received earlier this evening?*

Mark 1 **Strange Assistance** in your Campaign Log. Someone just saved your life.

At various points during this scenario, you will be asked to *record the time* next to entries in your Campaign Log. To do this, simply record, in brackets, the current agenda number and the number of doom on the current agenda. *For example: If there is 4 doom on agenda 1a, you would record the time as (1,4).*

### <black>Gaining and Losing Actions

As time becomes increasingly unstable, the number of actions you may take on a turn may also change.

<bullet><emsp>Several effects refer to standard actions. A standard action is

any action that does not have a limitation on its use, regardless

of its source. *For example, Finn Edwards has a copy of Leo De

Luca in play. He has four standard actions on his turns---the

default three and an additional action from Leo—as well as an

additional, non-standard action from his investigator ability

that can only be used to evade.*

<bullet><emsp>Each investigator is considered to gain their actions for the next

round in step 4.2 of the upkeep phase. This means that effects

after an investigator's turn cannot make them lose actions for

the next round, unless they happen after the the upkeep phase.

*For example, Finn Edwards is attacked by a Chronophage in

the enemy phase. This would cause him to lose an action, but as

his turn has ended he has no actions remaining. During the

upkeep phase of the same round, he draws the weakness

Overzealous; if an encounter card drawn from this effect would

cause him to lose actions, this happens as normal.*

<bullet><emsp>If a player card effect (such as the Gold Pocket Watch) causes

the investigator phase to repeat, investigators are considered to

gain their actions for their turns at the start of the phase. If a

player card effect allows an investigator to take an additional

turn, they are considered to gain their actions at the start of that

turn.

### <black>Haunted

Haunted is an ability that appears on some locations. Each time an

investigator fails a skill test while investigating a location, after

applying all results for that skill test, that investigator must resolve all “**Haunted –**” abilities on that location.

A location is “haunted” for the purposes of other card effects if it has at least one "**Haunted –**” ability (printed or otherwise).

*You fall. Though fall is maybe the wrong word—fall implies a sense of* down. *You tumble through realities, flashes of years long past and dizzying futures muddling your senses. You feel sick, faint, close to passing out.

A sudden stillness. You lie on solid ground. It takes you a minute to pull yourself to your feet, and your head still pounds. You're in a forest. Not one that looks familiar, but it's something. It's reality.

A roar cuts through your musings, painfully loud. Three creatures burst from the foliage, screeching as they flee past you, lizard-like beasts almost as tall as you are. You watch them flee, turning back just in time to spot a colossal beast crushing the trees in front of you. It roars again, the sound pounding your bones to jelly, as it charges you...

*Time lies before you, an endless expanse of realities.

Even in the midst of your current mission, you're forced to take a moment to gawk. Everything that ever was, everything that ever will be, could be, is here, open to you like the pages of a book. The knowledge, the opportunity, the sheer beauty of it all... it's a lot to take in.

Still, the moment passes, and the beauty of the scene is marred somewhat by the formless presence rising above it. Aforgomon, god of the minutes and the cycles; an unfathomable being who seeks nothing less than to unmake everything you see here. Mount Hollyoke's disrupted ritual is the fulcrum through which Aforgomon can reach into your universe.

And between this cosmic force and the universe it seeks to annihilate... you. You suddenly feel very, very small.*

**Resolution 1:** *The end of time is an experience unlike any other. Everything will be still; any sense of movement or causality was gone. Everything that was or could be or never was will be happening now, inasmuch as 'now' would have any meaning here.

All times are one. Everything will be now. And here is were you were stuck, where you would have been made part of an unchanging tapestry of reality, where you could be, would be, were, are, will be trapped forever. That is, if forever still existed.*

<bullet><emsp> In your Campaign Log, record that *all times are one.*

<bullet><emsp> Each investigator is driven **insane**.

<bullet><emsp> The investigators lose the campaign.

**Resolution 2:** *You find yourself, eventually, lying on a smooth, flat surface. Every inch of your body wants to sink into the floor, become one with the ground. You stay that way for a long, long time.

It's the smell of smoke that finally makes you pull yourself up. You're in the gymnasium of Mount Hollyoke Elementary School. The cultists and gangsters seem to be long gone, leaving behind only dormant runes and abandoned texts. The smoke drifts in from the rear door, so you exit out the front.

Day broke at some point, perhaps more than once. But you made it through, reality made it through, and perhaps, now, you can return to some semblance of normality. You've not lived that life for a year, sure, but you're the only you in the present now. You'll need to find somewhere new to live...

Lost in your thoughts, you watch as a conflagration consumes the school, presumably set by the backfiring ritual. This whole thing started with a fire; it seems only fitting that it should end the same way.*

<bullet><emsp> In your Campaign Log, record that *the investigators

<emsp> bound Aforgomon in a prison of time.*

<bullet><emsp> For each investigator who ended the game with at least 1

<emsp> copy of the Unspeakable Oath weakness in their hand,

<emsp> record in your Campaign Log that *'[investigator name]

<emsp> still bears Aforgomon's mark'.*

<bullet><emsp> In your Campaign Log, record the names of each

<emsp> investigator whose 'existence is waning'.

<bullet><emsp> The investigators win the campaign!

:::resolution

**Resolution 3:** *Time spins and whirls, which is an especially strange experience when you're standing outside it. Keeping a firm grip on the streams you're manipulating, you unwind the works of you and Aforgomon alike, until...

Time lies before you, an endless expanse of realities.

Everything that ever was, everything that ever will be, could be, is here, open to you like the pages of a book, reset to how it was before this fight begun. As Aforgomon's unholy presence once again looms above you, you let out a long breath, ready for round two.*

<bullet><emsp> Add 1 <elder_thing> token to the chaos bag. If you cannot, each

<emsp> investigator takes 1 mental trauma instead.

<bullet><emsp> The investigators must replay **Scenario VII: Time Runs

<emsp> Out**. Reset the game to this scenario’s Setup. Do not

<emsp> record anything else in your Campaign Log except for

<emsp> any trauma suffered from your previous game. No

<emsp> experience points are earned from your previous game.

<emsp> Players may not alter their decks, even if they are in an

<emsp> illegal state, or remove any weaknesses added during the

<emsp> scenario. Any player whose investigator was killed or

<emsp> driven insane is eliminated and may not choose a new

## Epilogue

**Check Campaign Log. In order, read each of the following

entries only if the investigators won the campaign and the

related campaign log entry is true.**

:::standalone

**Read the following only if at least one investigator's *existence is waning:***

*You're tired. This isn't exactly surprising; you just fought a god. As you wend your way through the early-morning Arkham streets, though, you feel surprisingly light on your feet---if fatigue weighs you down, this feeling lifts you up, until you're practically floating. You feel yourself drift off, still walking, into a cozy, endless sleep...*

Each investigator whose *existence is waning* is erased from reality. Remove that investigator's entry from your Campaign Log as thoroughly as possible, as that investigator never existed.

:::

:::standalone

**Read the following only if at least one surviving investigator *still bears Aforgomon's mark:***

*In the years that follow, you remain fascinated with time. After all, you understand spacetime perhaps better than anyone else alive. You try to share your findings a few times; each time, your theories are shot down as outlandish and unfounded. There's* so much* you could teach the world---you could advance the field of physics by decades with what you know---but nobody wants to listen.

Four years after your final confrontation with Aforgomon, you knock three times on the front door of an elegant manor on the outskirts of Arkham. A silent butler leads you to a bedchamber, where thick velvet curtains block out all light and the smell of death hangs heavy in the air. The rooms occupant stirs slightly.

"I'm so, so glad that you accepted my invitation." The voice is barely more than a whisper. The withered form of Joseph Baxter, the Myriad Gentleman, looks at least a hundred years old. He smiles at you, the predatory smile looking rather out of place on the old man's face. "We have much work to do."

:::standalone

**Read the following only if *you have advanced the schemes of the Silver Twilight Lodge:***

* "And we're quite certain it's real?" Carl Sanford's eyes rest on the slight man sat nervously before him. Mr. Sanford was an intimidating man at the best of times, but the intensity he was focusing on the messenger made the man want to shrink into nothingness.

"Y--- yes sir," he managed, "Our trials were conclusive. We now only miss one component-"

"Not quite. Our new friends helped us with that as well." Eyes twinkling, Sanford produces a loose array of singed papers from his desk. "After helping dispatch Baxter's operation, one of our agents recovered some of his research. We have everything we need.

"Let the great work begin."

## Design Notes

*Doctor Who* was a big part of my childhood. For a lot of reasons, most of which are irrelevant to this campaign, but the storyteller in me greatly appreciated the plot elements time travel allowed. The episode *Blink* is a great example of this (and a stellar watch, even if you know nothing about the show)---cause and effect does a merry little jig back and forth through time. Coming to design an Arkham Horror campaign in 2019, I settled on that as the core story I wanted to tell. It goes without saying that such a story is a lot more difficult to tell in an interactive medium than on a television show, but I hope I managed to convey the same feel.

Once I was playing with time travel, *Unstuck* was basically inevitable---I didn't want to fully dump the investigators in another time period, but I like cake and I love eating it, so I devoted a scenario to messing around with different time periods. I love more open-ended scenarios like *Threads of Fate,* so *A Year to Plan* happened. The Myriad Gentleman came to me in a dream, and actually predated the Swarming mechanic—he used to search for another copy of himself when he was drawn, and then *The

Dream-Eaters* was released and I stole that mechanic so damn quick. And then his scenario doesn't even use it. Hey ho. I ended up on seven scenarios simply because I didn't have any ideas for an eighth that weren't blatant filler.

Aforgomon was actually quite a late addition—there was always an ancient one looking to destroy time, but it was a long time before I actually did some research into appropriate Great Old Ones, and found Aforgomon. This is why for the most part there aren't any references to *The Chain of Aforgomon*---for the most part, it wasn't source material. Apologies to Clark Ashton Smith fans.

I had a blast designing this campaign, and I hope you enjoyed playing it. I imagine there are a ton of revisions still to come on this campaign, but in the meantime my mind drifts inexorably towards the next new idea. So now I've designed a fairly 'classic' Arkham campaign, I'm off to make something sprawling and break every rule I can think of. Given how long this one took me, expect something exciting in the early 2030s!

<right>--- Olivia Juliet</right>
